title: FALA: Locality-Aware PIM-Host Cooperation for Graph Processing with Fine-Grained Column Access
problem: Graph processing exhibits irregular memory access patterns that cause significant memory bandwidth waste on DRAM architectures: cache-based graph tiling suffers from overfetching due to the mismatch between DRAM burst size and the sparse data actually needed, while PIM-based approaches fail to exploit cache locality for high-reuse workloads.
method: FALA is a hybrid architecture integrating PIM and cache-based acceleration. It introduces a fine-grained column access mechanism within DRAM memory banks that allows selective access to individual columns (vertices) rather than fetching full DRAM rows, eliminating overfetching for sparse graph accesses. A locality-aware PIM architecture is designed to route accesses: high-reuse vertex data is served through the host CPU cache hierarchy, while low-reuse, irregular accesses are processed near-memory via PIM. The design minimizes unnecessary memory traffic while fully utilizing both internal DRAM bandwidth and on-chip caches.

title: Logic Restructuring with Preserved Logic Blocks
problem: Technology-independent logic optimization over-decomposes complex cells (adders, multiplexers) that should be preserved for technology mapping, degrading final PPA results.
method: Proposes 'boxing' logic blocks before optimization and preserving them during resubstitution. Transparent-boxing leverages information about boxed logic for better optimization than black-boxing, using wire-based resubstitution to optimize boxed networks while maintaining structure.

title: MLP-Offload: Multi-Level, Multi-Path Offloading for LLM Pre-training to Break the GPU Memory Wall
problem: LLM training blocked by GPU memory limits; existing offloading has high I/O overhead in training critical path
method: Multi-level, multi-path offloading engine; optimizer state across tiers; cache-efficient, contention-aware design

title: RTX 5090: Designed for the Age of Neural Rendering
problem: Neural rendering—combining classical graphics pipelines with learned neural networks—requires massive parallelism for real-time 3D rendering, shadow computation, and complex material simulation; RTX 5090 targets this emerging workload.
method: RTX 5090 combines NVIDIA's Ada/Hopper-generation streaming multiprocessor architecture with enhanced Tensor cores optimized for low-precision inference, improved memory bandwidth via next-generation interconnects, and specialized hardware for ray tracing and neural network evaluation.

title: 37.3 Monolithic in-Memory Computing Microprocessor for End-to-End DNN Inferencing in MRAM-Embedded 28nm CMOS Technology with 1.1Mb Weight Storage
problem: DNN inference on always-on AI sensors requires ultra-low power during both computation and idle phases; prior in-memory computing (IMC) works focused only on individual crossbar arrays, insufficient for complete DNNs.
method: A monolithic MRAM-embedded microprocessor integrates analog matrix multiplications via MRAM crossbar arrays with co-located weight storage (1.1Mb total), enabling end-to-end DNN inference without external weight fetching.

title: Multicore Environment State Representation for Agent-Directed Test Generation
problem: Verification of multicore systems requires testing core interactions, but current test generation lacks an effective method to extract actionable state information from raw environment observations for learning-based optimization.
method: A reinforcement learning approach where an RL agent generates test programs executed in a multicore simulation environment (16 and 32-core ARMv8 with MOESI coherence). The agent learns from interaction how to improve verification coverage by recovering structured state information from raw environment observations.

title: Extended User Interrupts (xUI): Fast and Flexible Notification without Polling
problem: Intel's existing User Interrupt (UIPI) mechanism for fast user-space notification has correctness and performance limitations that prevent it from matching shared-memory polling latency while maintaining the efficiency of asynchronous notification. Current designs lack support for preemption in user-level runtimes, kernel-bypass timers, and efficient interrupt forwarding to accelerators.
method: xUI extends Intel's UIPI model with four hardware mechanisms: (1) tracked interrupts that allow senders to know when an interrupt was delivered, (2) hardware safepoints that let user-level runtimes implement preemption without kernel involvement, (3) a kernel-bypass timer for deadline-driven scheduling, and (4) interrupt forwarding to route notifications directly to accelerators (modeled on Intel's DSA). The design is modeled and evaluated in gem5 full-system simulation, measuring end-to-end latency for three distinct use cases.

title: Integrating and Characterizing HPC Task Runtime Systems for hybrid AI-HPC workloads
problem: Hybrid AI-HPC workflows bottlenecked by Slurm srun throughput; srun unsuitable for dynamic heterogeneous tasks
method: RADICAL-Pilot integrated with Flux and Dragon runtime systems; hierarchical resource management

title: InfScaler: Enabling Efficient ML Inference Serving on Multi-Accelerator Edge Devices via Asymmetric Auto-Scaling
problem: Multi-accelerator edge SoCs with heterogeneous compute units (CPU, GPU, NPU, TPU) are poorly utilized by existing inference frameworks that lack bottleneck awareness and cannot efficiently partition models across diverse accelerators.
method: Discovers architectural bottleneck of ML models through profiling, designs bottleneck-aware asymmetric auto-scaling to allocate resources unequally to different model stages, leverages unified memory in edge SoCs for efficient data sharing between asymmetrically scaled partitions.

title: Misam: Machine Learning Assisted Dataflow Selection in Accelerators for Sparse Matrix Multiplication
problem: SpGEMM accelerators that support multiple dataflows (e.g., row-wise, column-wise, inner-product) face two critical problems: (1) no fast principled mechanism exists for selecting the optimal dataflow at runtime given input matrix sparsity patterns, and (2) providing hardware flexibility for multiple dataflows incurs area overhead and underutilization when one dataflow is locked in.
method: Misam uses a lightweight decision tree classifier to dynamically predict the optimal SpGEMM hardware configuration from matrix structural features (sparsity density, distribution, pattern statistics) extracted at runtime. To overcome hardware underutilization from multi-dataflow support, Misam targets FPGAs and exploits FPGA partial reconfigurability to deploy specialized, resource-efficient bitstreams tailored to specific sparsity regimes on demand. A reconfiguration engine evaluates whether the anticipated performance gain from switching bitstreams exceeds the reconfiguration overhead before triggering a reconfiguration.

title: NVR: Vector Runahead on NPUs for Sparse Memory Access
problem: Sparse DNNs suffer from irregular memory access patterns causing high cache miss rates and stalls, negating computational benefits of sparsity when dealing with reduced wall-clock execution time.
method: NVR adapts runahead execution to NPU architecture as a decoupled, speculative, lightweight hardware sub-thread that runs ahead to prefetch data, reducing cache misses without requiring compiler support or algorithmic changes; operates with <5% hardware overhead.

title: Versatile Cross-platform Compilation Toolchain for Schrödinger-style Quantum Circuit Simulation
problem: Quantum circuit simulators are CPU/GPU-bound; existing tools (Qiskit, cuQuantum) lack cross-platform optimization and underutilize hardware for high-qubit simulations (30-32 qubits).
method: Cross-platform compilation toolchain (CAST) with sparsity-aware gate fusion to eliminate redundant qubits, LLVM IR vectorization for CPUs, PTX code generation for Nvidia GPUs. Automatically selects best fusion strategy and backend per platform.

title: REIS: A High-Performance and Energy-Efficient Retrieval System with In-Storage Processing
problem: The retrieval stage of RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a throughput bottleneck because Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) on large embedding databases incurs massive data movement between host and storage; existing In-Storage Processing (ISP) approaches use storage-agnostic ANNS algorithms, do not accelerate the subsequent data-fetch step, and require heavy SSD hardware modifications.
method: REIS co-designs the ANNS algorithm with ISP hardware inside the storage system to avoid host-storage data movement. It adopts an ISP-tailored ANNS algorithm that exploits the internal bandwidth and parallelism of NAND flash controllers without large hardware modifications. REIS additionally accelerates the data-retrieval step for items selected by ANNS, overlapping fetch and search computations. The system is designed to minimize changes to storage hardware while maximizing throughput.

title: PowerMove: Optimizing Compilation for Neutral Atom Quantum Computers with Zoned Architecture
problem: Neutral atom quantum computers (NAQCs) with zoned architectures (ZA) and qubit movement capabilities require coordinated gate scheduling, qubit positioning, atom movement, and inter-zone communication, but existing compilers cannot jointly optimize these dimensions, leading to poor fidelity and long execution times for quantum circuits.
method: PowerMove is a compiler for NAQCs that jointly optimizes gate scheduling, qubit positioning, atom movement, and inter-zone communication for zoned architectures. The compiler introduces new optimization passes that model atom movement as a first-class resource and explore movement strategies jointly with gate ordering. For NISQ applications, PowerMove significantly reduces the number of atom movements and inter-zone communications, while for FTQC (fault-tolerant quantum computing), it replaces physical qubits with logical qubits encoded in quantum error correction (QEC) codes and applies analogous optimization. The compilation algorithm is designed for both correctness and efficiency, achieving up to 216.9x compilation speedup over prior methods.

title: A 320×256 6.9mW 2.2mK-NETD 120.4dB-DR LW-IRFPA with Pixel-Paralleled Light-Driven 20b Current-to-Phase ADC
problem: Long-wavelength cryogenic infrared focal plane arrays (LW-IRFPA) require high dynamic range readout circuits (ROIC) to improve signal-to-noise ratio, but conventional current-voltage or current-frequency modulation rely on power-hungry analog circuits susceptible to interference and crosstalk from long data buses. Prior ROICs consume significant power in analog circuits and data transfer.
method: Pixel-paralleled light-driven current-to-phase ADC (IP-ADC) architecture with four key components: (1) light-current-controlled oscillator (LCO) modulator powered only by photocurrent without extra supply, (2) phase-reconstruction circuit with sub-phase extraction to enhance low-light performance and reduce quantization noise, (3) pixel-level 20-bit asynchronous gray-code counter for high equivalent full-well capacity, and (4) low-swing bus data transfer circuit to reduce transmission power and crosstalk. Fabricated in 0.18μm CMOS for a 320×256 array with 30μm pixel pitch and QWIP detectors.

title: A Cache Interaction Graph for Data Locality Optimization
problem: Cache efficiency optimization and root-cause diagnosis of cache inefficiencies in programs is difficult due to complex interactions between data access patterns and cache hierarchy
method: Track cache line evictions; measure temporal and spatial locality; classify cache miss types; visualize via Cache Interaction Graph; extend Cachegrind for variable-level analysis
